notes.title: Steam Ealy Access release date changed
notes.notes: [p]Hi everyone! We are working very hard to release Multiverse Designer as soon as possible, and we can't wait to put it in your hands and see what amazing creations you come up with. Unfortunately, development has slowed over the last weeks and things aren't at the state that we expected, so we won't be able to meet the original release date of Late Q2.[/p][p][/p][p]We want to reassure you that it isn't a matter of being stuck in any specific roadblock: we just need more time to put the final work in the Early Access version of Multiverse Designer, particularly to implement some rules with Criteria, a painstaking work that takes a lot of our time. Our backers and beta testers can attest to the state of Multiverse Designer, and that the core product is already fully usable. The new expected release date is September; we are confident that Multiverse Designer will be ready for its Early Access release by then. We will let you know the specific date very soon. [/p][p][/p][p]In the meantime, we invite you to join us in our [url="https://discord.gg/gDFHARKSWa"]Discord server[/url], where you can learn more about the development of Multiverse Designer and see our ongoing development efforts.[/p][p] [/p][p]Thanks for your patience and support! [/p]

notes.title: Multiverse Designer will release on Early Access very soon!
notes.notes:
Hi everyone! We’ve got some big news to share with you, so let’s cut to the chase: [b]Multiverse Designer will release on Steam Early Access in Late Q2[/b] – that is, later this quarter! Very soon Multiverse Designer will be open to everyone. 

Now, this does not mean that we consider our virtual tabletop to be finished, or this one to be the version that we promised our backers when we did the Kickstarter campaign. Opening our doors to all users represents a great opportunity to[b] gather some very useful feedback, [/b]test our strengths and limits, and of course potentially get more resources to keep growing Multiverse Designer even more. But [b]we want to assure our backers that this Early Access release does not change our development priorities, [/b]and we will keep working towards the Full Release version of Multiverse Designer as hard as always. 

Mind you, despite acknowledging that there are still features we have to work for us to move on to Full Release (like the anticipated Asset Spawner or more rulesets implemented in Criteria), Multiverse Designer is pretty much feature-complete as it is – in the sense that[b] it is fully usable and stable. The Map Creator is finished,[/b] with almost 10,000 3D assets available for all kinds of settings, from fantasy to sci-fi, modern, cyberpunk, or Victorian. [b]The Cutscene Editor is also finished,[/b] and you can already [b]create and play online games[/b] with your friends in the maps you create (or download from Steam Workshop). 

[previewyoutube=QOENwgF00Yw;full][/previewyoutube]

Criteria is still in development, but [b]we are working to release with the basic D&D 5ed ruleset implemented,[/b] so the system can take care of all the rules-tracking and bookkeeping for you. Other systems will come further down the line (and we know some community members are also working hard to implement their favorite games, such as GURPS!) 

There’s an important detail that we want to explain.[b] Multiverse Designer will release as a free download on Steam, in a limited version[/b] that allows only to join other people’s games as a player, as well as a limited version of the Map Creator and Cutscene Editor with a small number of assets for you to play around. [b]The complete Multiverse Designer, the Game Master edition, [/b]which gives unrestricted access to all assets and allows you to create and direct multiplayer games as a GM, [b]will be a DLC, available as an in-game purchase. [/b]It is the best solution we have found to make Multiverse Designer as accessible and easy to use as possible, without any potential server issues. 

We want to thank you for staying with us all this time; we hope you keep supporting us when we release on Early Access.[b] We can’t wait to see what you are able to do with Multiverse Designer. [/b]We will let you know very soon more details about what we are working on for the next update, which will arrive along with the Early Access release. Until then, happy adventuring!

notes.title: February Update is here!
notes.notes:
Hi everyone! We're very happy to report that we just released [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1068500/view/545601235427786817]the anticipated new update that we recently talked you about[/url]. It's one of the most important updates since we made the beta available to backers: you'll finally be able to[b] play in the maps you have created with Multiverse Designer! [/b]

As we already explained, along with the gameplay module we're implementing[b] the first rules created with Criteria, [/b]although they're still very basic: rolling dice, HP and initiative tracking, movement, basic actions, character sheet editing, up to 20 common skills, and 3 spells. There's lots of work to do in terms of implementing rulesets, but at least now you can play and have the computer do the basic bookkeeping for you. This update also [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1068500/view/510698874256494070]implements the Character Forge; check out how to access it[/url] in our latest post (and do send us your creations, you can get an extra invite to the beta!) 

As you know, this update also comes with two ready-to-play encounters: a fight against a wyvern (we recorded ourselves playing it, you can watch it [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1068500/view/510698874256490687]here[/url]) for the duration of the Steam Next Fest; we'll update it to Youtube when it's over). The second fight is against a group of humanoid enemies. We have also implemented [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1068500/view/517452371461144964]tutorials[/url] to help with the landing -- Multiverse Designer is a powerful tool with many features that can be overwhelming at first, so we hope these tutorials can help with feeling the ropes of our tool. And finally, the Campaigns, a way to create an overall script for an entire module or campaign, as we also explained [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1068500/view/545601235427786817]here[/url]. 

Along with these new major features, we've also worked on improving stability and quashing some rebellious bugs; you'll see a more detailed changelog below these lines. That's all for today! See you on our [url=https://steamcommunity.com/linkfilter/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fdiscord.gg%2FCtZ7YQAUum]Discord[/url]server -- you can also follow us on [url=https://www.instagram.com/toopangames/]Instagram[/url] and now [url=https://bsky.app/profile/multiversedesigner.bsky.social]Bluesky[/url]. See you in our next update! 

PS: Remember that [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1068500/announcements/detail/517451737842319532]we have sent you the Steam keys[/url] that will unlock your Kickstarter exclusive content further down the road. Please check your inbox and spam folders, and send us a DM through Kickstarter if you can't find them, so we can re-send them to you. Have a nice day! 

[h3][b]CHANGELOG[/b][/h3]
[list]
[*] First version of Criteria
[*] First version of the gameplay module (create and join campaigns to play together)
[*] Character Forge: Avatar and character sheets editors 
[*] New animations for the Character Forge character
[*] Basic in-game tutorials
[*] Full Steam Workshop integration
[*] New assets from Kitbash3D (Atlantis, Shogun e Shangrila)
[*] Several fixes in character animations and collisions
[*] Several fixes in the asset search tags
[*] Kickstarter add-ons badges are now showed in the main menu along with the tier badge (keys must have been redeemed for that)
[*] Terrain bases on some assets can now be customized or turned invisible
[/list]

notes.title: New update coming, and Multiverse Designer comes to Steam Next Fest
notes.notes:
Hey everyone! We’re happy to announce that [b]there's a new update coming, and with some very anticipated features. [/b]It’s been a very busy month (you’ll see why), but this update is going to be one of the most important in a good while.

The next update implements gameplay – at last,[b] you will be able to play in the maps you create or download! [/b]It also comes with the first Criteria rules (so Multiverse Designer automatizes some of the bookkeeping and rules for you), although both things are still limited and a work-in-progress. Basically, [b]we have implemented basic D&D-like rules:[/b] rolling dice, HP and initiative tracking, full character sheet editing, basic and special attacks, over 20 common skills (Hide, Spot, and many others) and 3 spells, namely fireball, lightning bolt, and cone of cold. It also includes [b]two ready-to-play encounters – one against a wyvern and a second against humanoid monsters. [/b]And of course, if you want to do the bookkeeping and rules-tracking yourself, you can already play on any map you have created or downloaded.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42436016/663e754a0ed800722a81e2b3e9b540640e280a41.png[/img]

The second new feature that we have implemented is the ability to [b]customize your in-game avatar: that is, you’ll be able to create a character in the Character Forge,[/b] customizing its face and body as well as its character sheet tied to a specific set of rules (because obviously a D&D character sheet is quite different from, say, a sheet for Call of Cthulhu). Players can do this offline at their own pace, and it will be shared with their Game Masters when they connect to an online game. Then, when you play your character model will be the avatar you have created. 

There’s another new feature coming that is meant to make Game Masters’ life easier. We call it Campaigns: basically, it’s [b]a way for GMs to create an overall script of an adventure[/b] (or, well, a whole campaign). When you create a game you decide which ruleset you’ll be using, what maps it will include, what encounters players will face… You can think of it as how a pen-and-paper book presents a campaign: it describes the special rules, the locations, the NPCs… In the case of Multiverse Designer, it can be as simple or as complex as you want – you can set it as a loose guide or as a very detailed script of how the adventure will evolve. 

[b]This new update is expected to drop by the end of this month.[/b] We’re looking forward to seeing your first games on Multiverse Designer! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42436016/dbc7f86fa93e551f0171a00d5a68114265c465fc.png[/img]

[h3]Multiverse Designer comes to the Steam Next Fest![/h3]

As we just said it’s been particularly busy as of lately, because we didn’t just work on all these new features – [b]we’re also taking part in the upcoming Steam Next Fest,[/b] so we had to work on creating [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1068660/Multiverse_Designer_Demo/]a demo for Multiverse Designer[/url] as well (as you need a free demo to take part in the festival). We didn’t want this opportunity to become a distraction, in the sense of delaying the development and delivery of new features to you backers, so we decided that the easiest course of action would be to make a demo out of the beta version backers have. It will be available for a very short time, though – so [b]if you want to nudge some friends to try Multiverse Designer for free[/b] (and who knows, maybe even play a game with them!), do it fast, because in a month or so we’ll take it down! Mind you, if you want to play online with somebody who’s not a backer, both of you will have to use the demo version. Due to how the Steam backend works, there is no crossplay between different “games” – and for Steam, a game and its demo are different applications. 

And now that we have announced we’ll take part in the Steam Next Fest, we want to ask for your help just one more time. As you know, we’re a small team developing a very big and ambitious tool. We need every bit of promotion, every opportunity under the spotlight if we want Multiverse Designer to grow for many years, even above the original vision of the Kickstarter campaign – and helping us with that is as easy as important: [b]please share our demo and ask your friends to wishlist us on Steam[/b] (if you want to take an extra step or play with some friends, you can download it too!). It’s as simple as that. During the Next Fest, the more people download the demo and wishlist the game, the more publicity Steam gives us; this event can be a make-or-break occasion for any game, much more for a tool such as ours, which let us tell you it’s not easy to promote – there aren’t that many media outlets or influencers who talk about virtual tabletops! So, [b]by spreading the word, you can make a world of a difference – every single download and wishlist counts. [/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42436016/200deccaf07d66f0da4210095a03d225c82f37b0.png[/img]

Thanks in advance for your help. See you on our [url=https://steamcommunity.com/linkfilter/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fdiscord.gg%2FCtZ7YQAUum]Discord[/url]server, and make sure to share your creations if you have access to the beta or when you download the demo – we can’t wait to see what you can do with Multiverse Designer!  You can also follow us on [url=https://www.instagram.com/toopangames/]Instagram[/url] and now [url=https://bsky.app/profile/multiversedesigner.bsky.social]Bluesky[/url]. See you in our next update! 

PS: Remember that [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1068500/announcements/detail/517451737842319532]we have sent you the Steam keys[/url] that will unlock your Kickstarter exclusive content further down the road. Please check your inbox and spam folders, and send us a DM through Kickstarter if you can't find them, so we can re-send them to you. Have a nice day!

notes.title: September Update is live!
notes.notes:
Hi everyone! Today we’re releasing a new update for the Multiverse Designer beta. As we already explained, for this update we focused mostly on working on the assets, both adding new collections and improving the user experience of the ones already implemented. [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1068500/Multiverse_Designer/]In that previous post[/url] we went into detail about the assets included in this update – [b]mostly for modern settings, but also vehicles[/b] (cars, trucks, and fantasy vehicles like carriages and chariots). 

In this vein, [b]we added highways, military vehicles, and over 100 modern and sci-fi character models, like soldiers.[/b] With all these new assets and our Cutscene Editor you can set a scene where, for instance, players are thrown from a jeep into a bombed highway, sieged by tanks, forcing them to run for their lives to the nearest trench. Talk about an exciting in media res beginning!

[previewyoutube=yGxZDuall4U;full][/previewyoutube]

On top of that, we have reviewed all our previous assets: [b]we have fixed errors in over 2,000 assets such as positioning problems,[/b] windows floating in the air, invisible sides and texture glitches. We have also corrected the size of all the assets so you don’t inadvertently plant streetlights the size of the Empire State Building. The movement algorithm now works correctly, no matter the size of the assets in the map. We reviewed the tags of all the previously implemented objects, and added several new tags, to make it easier for you to find what you’re looking for. 

We also included new foliage objects, a fancy way of calling grass, trees, and bushes that you can now add to the map (so you’re not limited by the flora already present in the level when it spawns).There are also new candle lighting assets, all of them now have fire and turn on and off. On top of that, [b]you can create text assets and place them anywhere on the map,[/b] useful as notes or even descriptions for you to read as the Game Master. For a better user experience, assets now have names that can seen by clicking the I(nfo) button.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42436016/3dca45521426f44519092d3ab8e40f00160c2663.jpg[/img]

And finally (when it comes to assets), [b]you can now import assets or maps created in Multiverse Designer by other users,[/b] importing them in the same place where they were saved. This allows multiple people to work on the same map and then simply import the other person's work and it will be exactly where they put it. Handy, huh? 

And last, but not least…[b] we have created some new maps for you to use[/b] – as inspiration, to copy sections of it for your own maps and games, or directly to place your adventures within its confines. We have created [b]a modern war zone,[/b] for military adventures set from the 20th century to present day; as well as [b]a modern city with classic elements[/b] (think of a European capital). But our two favorites in this update are the [b]Cyberpunk Waterfall[/b] – the largest city we have created so far – and the one we call “A dark and stormy night”: [b]a fantasy/Gothic horror setting[/b] that will be the delight of Ravenloft, Call of Cthulhu and other horror games players.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42436016/96df5103d91eab2b956a53a8d3f59c5d9eab25d8.jpg[/img]

What do you think about all these new assets? When you start using them in Multiverse Designer, please spare a minute to [b]send us your creations through [url=https://discord.gg/CtZ7YQAUum]Discord[/url] or our social media[/b] – we can’t wait to see what you do! Also, friendly reminder to all our backers: [b]please redeem your Steam key as soon as you can,[/b] and if you haven’t received yours, send us a DM on Kickstarter or email us to info@toopangames.com. 

In our next post update, we will discuss in more detail what we are working on for the near future. Stay tuned!

notes.title: July Beta Update is now available!
notes.notes:
Hi everyone! Today, we’re releasing [b]a new update that includes some new features of certain importance,[/b] fixes for reported bugs, and some quality-of-life improvements. The most relevant of these new features is the inclusion of[b] auto-saving [/b]– we know firsthand how maddening it is to lose your work due to a power outage or computer crash (oh gosh, how much we wish we didn’t), and that’s something we don’t want you to experience, so this was something we wanted to implement as soon as possible. 

We’re also including some [b]new shortcuts[/b] (check the patch notes below for more details), [b]new maps that use objects from the Enterable collections[/b] (that is, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1068500/view/4219387168552306309]the interactive buildings[/url]), and [b]tags for lots of objects and assets[/b]. Again, please check the patch notes for all the details – we really recommend you read them carefully so you don’t miss anything. 

This new version also implements[b] the first parts of Criteria, the scripting language [/b]that Multiverse Designer will use to create and automatize rules for your tabletop rpgs. Now you can create character sheets and tables, as well as import and export tables to any spreadsheet editor. Mind you, this is still in alpha version. That means that it’s not just rough around the edges: there might be issues and unexpected problems, and data filled now might get lost, or just not be compatible with future versions of Criteria. Use with caution! If you want to give it a go, you can find tutorials about Criteria [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3SMOgIXXl1o&list=PLrtuAu0kHUOktDDd_wscqRzjv95bPkRlx]on our Youtube channel[/url], and you can always [url=https://discord.gg/CtZ7YQAUum]drop by our Discord server[/url] to ask questions. 

Having said that, here are the full patch notes for this update. We hope you enjoy it! 

[h3][b]New features/content[/b][/h3]

[list]
[*] This is the first version of MD containing a part of the Criteria language. You can create character sheets and tables. You can import and export tables to any spreadsheet editor. THIS IS AN ALPHA VERSION. Data filled in this version may be lost or not compatible with future versions
[*] Alt + M now also hides the red warning messages;
[*] Inclusion of the Alt + W shortcut to hide only the red warning messages while keeping the screen icons
[*] The object that loads textures comes by default listing only .png files;
[*] New user preferences menu on the main screen (for now only for the Autosave options)
[*] Autosave (with the possibility of customizing the saving frequency and the number of history files, values ​​filled in the new user preferences menu)
[*] Weather effects are now applied to the trees, grasses and plants of the Jungle level (the weather effects for the landscape itself still need to be included, it will be done in a future version)
[*] Specific tag included for the horse saddle object
[*] Specific tag included for the spline wall object
[*] Rampart tag included for all walls
[*] Tags included to identify Kitbash3D sets (Valhalla, Iron Forge, Medieval Siege, Outpost, Neo SanFrancisco, Secret Lab, Dark Fantasy, Medieval Market, Art Nouveau, Victorian, Ancients and Future Warfare)
[*] Added a new button on the object properties screen that shows its general information (unique identifier number, size and linked tags)
[*] New messages for the map loading screen (thanks for all the suggestions!)
[*] Added new maps that use objects from the Enterables collection (Eastern, Mesoamerica, Jungle, Wild West and Old Desert New)
[*] The cutscene spline can now be selected by clicking on the yellow spline path
[*] New objects placed on the map will always appear over the landscape
[/list]

[h3][b]Fixed bugs[/b][/h3]

[list]
[*] Fixed a bug in the spline wall object that caused the height of one of the sides of the spline to not be saved
[*] Correction in the arch with floor object
[*] Correction in the gothic cathedral object (floating boards)
[*] Fixed a bug that caused cube objects placed on a map overlapping other objects to lose the scale changes made when loading the map
[*] Modification to not allow the scale in all directions gizmo to be used on objects that cannot be scaled in all directions
[*] Fixed a bug that closed the game when saving a map with an object using the landscape blend texture on a level with landscape (for example, the Jungle) and trying to open it in the Dungeon level
[*] Alternative to minimize the impact of a bug that sometimes leaves the object preview thumbnail always open - now, if it occurs, when clicking on any of the object menu buttons, the thumbnail should disappear
[*] Fixed a bug that left some stones "blue" when they were close to or below the grid line
[*] Correction in the textures of some tent and cloth objects so they can be seen from both sides
[*] Correction of the “grass disabler” object so that it works in the Forest, Castle and Jungle
[*] Fixed a bug that could cause a map to fail to load in some situations
[*] Fixed a bug that could cause copied objects to be created under the landscape
[*] Fixed a bug that could cause water/lava objects to have a distorted texture or even disappear when scaled
[*] Correction in some object pivots (trash can, wall and water)
[*] Correction in some door objects
[*] Merged Tags "Walls" into "Wall"
[*] Correction in the appearance of some trees in the Castle level
[/list]

notes.title: Beta version 1.0 just released!
notes.notes:
Hi everyone! We've great news: we're very excited to announce that a new version of the Multiverse Designer beta is now available to all our beta testers. [b]This build includes the Map Creator and Cutscene Editor, and we consider it to be our version 1.0[/b] – which means that, if we don't find any critical bugs that require major overhauls (something that hasn't happened so far),[b] we will make it available to all backers very soon![/b]

We will need some time after our beta testers put their hands on this new build to decide on a release date, so stay tuned to our social media channels ([url=http://www.instagram.com/toopangames]Instagram[/url] and [url=https://twitter.com/ToopanGames]Twitter[/url]) and [url=https://discord.gg/7vvmMpgEVF]Discord server[/url]. Hopefully [b]within a few days we will be able to announce the specific release date to all our backers[/b] of the Map Creator and Cutscene Editor. While that happens, not to hype you up or anything, but here’s a list of all the new content and fixes implemented in this new build…

[h3][b]New features/content[/b][/h3]

[list]
[*] New Kitbash3D assets included (from the Iron Forge, Ancients, Valhalla, Cyber District, Neo San Francisco and Medieval Siege collections)
[*] New way to texture objects to blend in with the Landscape (new environment called @Landscape Blend)
[*] Creation of base assets for structures already integrated with the merge with Landscape (new environment called @Landscape Blend)
[*] Two new levels with 64km2 included - Desert and Rocky Hills
[*] New Dystopic Desert map (saved in the Desert level)
[*] New tags for assets (used in the search bar)
[*] Inclusion of the new Evil Watcher character
[*] Use of the special character $ at the beginning of the name of Toopan maps (so, from now on, it will not be possible to save maps with the name starting with the $ character)
[*] Added some "indoors" to many assets of "building" categories (Houses, buildings, etc) making them no longer transparent while looking from inside them
[*] Character Forge asset moved to the Tools category in the assets menu
[*] Included "jump" action to all controllable characters
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42436016/5a56e73358326da1b31bbd8fbee3e7d58ca5a0d1.png[/img]

[h3][b]Performance optimization[/b][/h3]

[list]
[*] Optimization of lights on the map with automatic enabling and disabling according to distance
[*] Optimization of video memory usage
[*] Texture optimization and possibility of using assets with up to 4 million triangles, benefiting users with video cards with less memory
[*] LOD adjustments  in several objects to improve performance
[*] Separation of all objects into opaque and transparent in order to use the full potential of Nanite.
[*] Jungle level performance tweaks and optimization
[*] Optimization for loading large maps, and addition of progress bar
[*] Performance optimization  of assets that have lights (torches, candles, chandeliers, etc.)
[*] Performance optimization and progress bar creation for the dungeon generator
[/list]

[h3][b]Fixed bugs[/b] [/h3]

[i]Thanks to all our beta testers for reporting these bugs![/i]

[list]
[*] Fixed a bug where when you selected the "parent" assets  in a group, you couldn't select the others
[*] Fixed a bug where some doors didn't disappear when their layer wasn't visible
[*] Fixed a bug where some books were misaligned
[*] Fixed a bug where the game crashed due to the lack of keyframes while making a cutscene
[*] Fixed an interaction with layers and groups where some of them were working in an unexpected way
[*] Fix with the shadow of certain assets in situations of intense light ("glitching" shadows)
[*] Fixed a problem when opening the save/load maps window (it was possible to open the window again even though it was still open)
[*] Correction of rotation and pivots of several assets
[*] Bug fix where when loading a map, it could have the weather effects that were applied to the map that was previously loaded
[*] Bug fix where the message "###HoveringMuro != nullptr in ADungeonPawn::DPawnMouseMove" could appear when loading a map while another is already loaded
[*] Fixed an issue where an error could occur when trying to load a very large map with another very large map already loaded
[*] Fixed the colision with stairs, that now, allow characters to use them correctly
[/list]

notes.title: Dev Diary #4: Dev update
notes.notes:
Hi everyone! These last few weeks, we’ve been hard at work, mostly improving performance and overall smoothness but also implementing new assets. [b]You can see below some cool screenshots of the new maps [/b]we have put into Multiverse Designers – although if you follow us [url=https://x.com/ToopanGames]on Twitter[/url] or [url=https://www.instagram.com/toopangames/]Instagram[/url] you might have already seen them (we've posted some more over there as of lately, go check it out!) 

Wait a second – you don’t follow us on social media? Alright, go there and do it now. We’ll wait for you. Here are the screenshots in the meantime (click on the images to enlarge them). 

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42436016/f5f0c2198bd3838f58f807d037ec2ac036aadbf2.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42436016/263970bf5f1a1d371a0c46d708c796b2d6a58236.jpg[/img][/url] [url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42436016/ed378383a61236ede8d63f34bfdd4a942f42bcc8.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42436016/d4bf246c3a56466fd1fca67cd3b4dba138b811a9.jpg[/img][/url]

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42436016/eab94eac467267db7230d74eeb8c91c370d412c2.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42436016/46a5651cf0178450d0878fbecf551a6c00ef970e.jpg[/img][/url] [url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42436016/ec51031c726c45701c38abb773a6eee1589f3ff0.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42436016/a91eaa32e2f35916f614a3d9f9bd0bae9a027d5a.jpg[/img][/url]

Done now? Alright, we can go on then. As I was saying, we’ve been working on optimization, and this is already making a noticeable difference, resulting in a more seamless and enjoyable game. That’s not to say we have not had some setbacks, though. We updated Multiverse Designer to Unreal Engine 5.4, its latest version, which can be significantly faster; but it created serious stability problems, and[b] after extensive testing we decided to roll it back to UE 5.3. [/b]This version is much more reliable, and we think getting a 5% increase in speed (just a placeholder number) is not worth a less stable version.

But we are still way ahead of schedule – by launching the beta early, we have had more time to gather valuable feedback and make necessary improvements; and despite the setbacks we have experienced, everything is still on track to releasing Multiverse Designer to all backers in the near future. While we work on the other features that will come in the next updates,  we ask to everyone tho stay tuned --[b]in the next month we will be releasing the first stable version to all our backers[/b]! 

[b]Thanks to all our community for your continued support[/b] – we can’t wait to put Multiverse Designer in your hands and see what you create with it!

notes.title: DEVELOPMENT UPDATE
notes.notes:
Welcome back designers! This week we decided to bring you some updates. We thought we'd spend a little time explaining to you some of our most common functions and how to change a map to make your [b]worldbuilding as easy as possible.[/b] That's why we brought some explanations about the interactions you will have using the multiverse designer!

[h2][b]ADD NEW OBJETCS![/b][/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42436016/567885a4ae162934ead592ec6fadfdf94f1fb84c.gif[/img]

You can browse through our menu and find the most varied groups of assets including houses, castles, trees and plants and they can be changed using gizmos at their ends, [b]changing their proportions and diversifying their size,[/b] rotating them or even changing the thickness at will, this way you will have the ability to stake them and make piles thus creating unique assets or more than one floor in a single map.

  Any group of assets can be joined and grouped, these groups can allow you to [b]change the proportions and dimensions of all objects at the same time[/b] making them grow and change equally without losing the sync or proportion between them.

 Many of these assets have the ability to change color or even material, they also react differently with the lights on or off, therefore increasing the variation of each object; we currently have [b]more than 5.000 assets [/b]and each one with its multiple variations exponentially increasing the number of assets.

[h2][b]CHANGING PROPORTIONS...[/b][/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42436016/a910e8c33f419fa69a4b10d292f41f1b541351ce.gif[/img]

You will also be able to stretch the walls or even the furniture so that they fit[b] perfectly in a place,[/b] being able to make maps extremely small or huge as you wish, allowing you not only, changing the objects completely, but also to make fine adjustments choosing the best details for them.

Multiverse designer even has a [b]magnetic alignment[/b] that can make quick and perfect adjustments without so much effort, this allows you to align objects on the grid without worrying about decimals or proportions.

[h2][b]...AND THE FLOORS...[/b][/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42436016/67dc93ad7d067cd473ac52aab453cb9fdbf26328.gif[/img]
 It is worth highlighting some specific tools such as the [b]polygonal floor, [/b]this floor allows you to create different formats from the conventional ones and fit it in the most different rooms, also giving you the ability to change the texture or even the effect of the floor, you can also import two-dimensional images to the game, being able to create even more textures for your dungeons.

[h2][b]... AND THE WALLS![/b][/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42436016/a491fa9bac369785be065bcaa944036c0d55d0e0.gif[/img]
Another tool that can be well used is the[b] curved walls [/b]tool, these walls allow you to curve them to both sides making not only circular rooms but also oval or elliptical rooms in addition to castle walls and being able to follow winding paths coasting even the more crooked edges
[h2]
[b]LIGHT ADJUSTMENT![/b][/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42436016/42250bb5aa997ca4a8cb69065687925779a21a77.gif[/img]
 The lighting edition also gives you  completely control and change the environment, being a key part for the climatization of the place, increasing the incidence of light or changing the color of the same can create infinite types of ambients, temperatures or environments, not only assets like torches, bonfires and fireplaces but magic effects will be [b]updated in real time [/b]too giving the feeling of greater immersion to your game.

 These are just some of the many features that the multiverse designer makes available to its users, many of these features are still under development and[b] will improve as the game progresses[/b], keep an eye out for the news on the social media, so you don't miss any updates!

[b][i]Good rolls and see y'all soon![/i][/b]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1068500/Multiverse_Designer/

notes.title: DEVELOPMENT UPDATE
notes.notes:
When you decide to play an RPG campaign, you and all other players are taking part in the creation of an fantastic alternate dimension which in everything is possible. A simulated reality, limited only by imagination.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42436016/f2d0f9222eb486dc8d70d18844cb8bbb9a64f676.png[/img]
Each and every set of rules present in an RPG book was created to simulate reality in this fantasical worlds and rolling the dice is only to help the experience be more immersive. every game has  rules to help with the imersion, but every setting needs has its own rules!

[list]
[*] A horror setting will present rules to keep track of characters’ sanity.
[*] A sci-fi setting will have different rules for lasers, holograms, force fields, or gravity.
[*] A fantasy setting will offer combat rules for melee or ranged weapons, armor, class, and magic.
[/list]

There are countless rules for an ever-growing list of categories.
As soon as we started working on Multiverse Designer, we realized that we want to have all that in the plataform, as much as possible so we envisioned a platform that could simulate all realities.
It was clear to us that Multiverse Designer should be an all-purpose tool capable of hosting any conceivable theme for a role-playing game but how can anyone create a simulation engine for systems that don’t even exist yet?
[u]Sounds ambitious, right? Well, challenge accepted![/u]

[h3][b]THE LAYERS OF CREATION[/b][/h3]
That's when we decided to develop an in-game algorithm that enables players to create and edit any RPG rule they can come up with.
A new language for processing RPG rules was born and its name is Criteria.
Our top priority was to offer players a quick-and-easy way to navigate the main elements present in most role-playing games:

[b][list]
[*] Tables
[/list][/b]
Like it or not, the easiest way to manage the overload of information within any RPG rulebook is through organized spreadsheets. Criteria is a lifesaver when it comes to quick access to attributes, skills, weapons, class, equipment, etc.

[b][list]
[*] Character Sheets
[/list][/b]
An in-depth character sheet with sub-divisions and custom tabs for different needs, such as a list of skills, features or spells. You can add anything relevant (or not) to the characters in your system.


[b][list]
[*] Full game automation
[/list][/b]
We also dislike these long combat scenes that were supposed to last no more than 30 seconds but end up taking half the game’s session. Criteria’s primary purpose is to speed up the game. All you have to do is choose your actions, roll the dice and watch the magic happens.

[b][list]
[*] Easy modding
[/list][/b]
Criteria is flexible enough to allow for easy modding, enabling players to simulate any RPG ever created. Past, present or future.
As we went through with Criteria’s development, we realized the size of the task we decided to undertake. It seemed impossible to come up with something easy to fill but at the same time communicate data and portray narrative. 
To be honest, it wasn’t a simple solution but we’re sure it was one worth the effort and by using tables, we manage that and anyone can edit system data. This means that all it takes to add a new spell, character or weapon is to fill up a spreadsheet row.

We also used spreadsheets to define game rules. With simple yet powerful expressions, you can create restrictions or possibilities for advantages through different game conditions.
The Barbarian class can learn the Rage skill at level 4, or only the Android race can make hyperspace jumps! All the possibilities are endless and you’re in control.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42436016/3db3f3dcb22636cfb32b39b781906aebe078b6b9.png[/img]

This is Criteria’s first layer of depth, which can be easily altered without any programming knowledge at all. We believe most customizations will happen through these simple spreadsheet modifications.
Criteria is a procedural language, partially object-oriented and enacted through a simulated computer inside Multiverse Designer.
That’s right, we had to create a mainframe inside the game with its own memory, commands and everything else, including line by line debugging. Watch out, Visual Studio, we’re coming for you!

[h3][b]Here’s a quick example:[/b][/h3]

If a party of three players is trying to hide from a group of four guards, each player would have to roll a Stealth skill test against each of the guards’ Perception points.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42436016/395e9c340d8370c594ee4da2591444589be2266e.png[/img]

Usually, the poor Game Master would have to compare each one of the players' numbers with each of the guards’. But when using Criteria, it’s easy to automate dice rolling for all kinds of situations.
In the above example, every dice to be rolled would appear directly on players’ screens, ready to determine the outcome of the situation in seconds. At the same time, four dice would instantly show up on the Game Master’s screen, ready to roll for the guards.
Then, Criteria would analyze relevant data from Character Sheets and apply results from everyone’s dice rolling instantly. The spreadsheets are used to execute system rules.
This is Criteria’s second layer of depth. It achieves automation and flexibility within any conceivable rule.
Here is a list of extra features to ease your game’s flow:
[list]
[*] Specific screens and forms for distinct actions.
[*][i]Special attacks, flanking, higher ground, etc.[/i]
[*] Confirmation screen for GMs initiated by player’s request.
[*] [i]Can I roll for diplomacy?[/i]
[*] Extra dice rolling for critical hits with double damage.
[*] All Criteria’s files are available to users, allowing for easy modding.
[*] Add new commands and rules at any time and grow your system as you go!
[*] Additional dice rolling for situations with strict rules, such as invisibility or concealment.
[*] Create your custom calendar with any timeframe for fiction worlds or other planes of reality.
[/list]
The same tools used by Toopan Games to create RPG rules in Multiverse Designer are available to all users. Anyone can easily customize an entire system or create a new one.
Multiverse Designer encourages players to dream high! This is a project directed to the modding community. We want players to share their creations, discover new ideas and be inspired to create.
What multiverses will you design?

Thanks for reading, and stay tuned for more updates! If you want to help us, Wishlist and Follow the game here on Steam -- and let your friends know about it!
